business_problem: ATB Financial needed to modernize critical SAP financial-reporting systems, reduce chronic overprovisioning, and standardize disaster recovery without sacrificing the performance and availability required for banking workloads.
solution_summary: ATB Financial expanded its Google Cloud footprint from analytics into SAP modernization by combining Compute Engine, Hyperdisk, BigQuery, Google Kubernetes Engine, and Google Cloud VMware Engine. Memory-optimized Compute Engine instances now run SAP HANA and broader finance and regulatory-reporting environments, while Hyperdisk Balanced supports newer M4-based workloads and other application tiers are mapped to N-series and C-series machines. GKE supports internally developed and commercial banking applications that exchange operational data with SAP systems, and BigQuery continues to accelerate analytics and reporting. The new model replaces long procurement cycles and 30–40% excess capacity with on-demand infrastructure, tiered storage, and custom machine types that better fit workload needs. The result is lower total cost of ownership, faster financial insight, and a disaster-recovery posture that fits ATB’s evolving banking strategy.

data_flow: SAP and banking workloads run on Compute Engine and Hyperdisk-backed storage, with banking applications on GKE exchanging operational data with those systems. Analytical and reporting outputs flow into BigQuery, and disaster-recovery environments are standardized with GCVE.
business_outcome: ATB reduced SAP infrastructure cost, improved reporting speed, and replaced overbuilt capacity planning with a more flexible cloud model that better matches banking workload demand.
